issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream in things_advanced.py is unexplained and load-bearing for the new test
issues.detail: The example silently swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different preconditions around Content-Length. The change is what makes the new 400 assertion pass, suggesting production code was bent to fit the test. No rationale or comment justifies the swap.

issues.description: FAQ example fabricates the 400 behavior it claims to demonstrate without stating the underlying contract
issues.detail: The PostTest handler manually reads req.content_length and returns 400 on empty read, then asserts this as Falcon behavior. The actual lesson (header override in simulate_post) is one line; the rest is scaffolding that teaches a wrong mental model. The Content-Length-vs-body-length contract is never named.

issues.description: README diff smuggles unrelated semantic changes under cosmetic reformatting
issues.detail: The README mixes typographic reflow with real semantic edits: StorageError.handle signature reorder (ex,req,resp -> req,resp,ex), str(status)+reason replaced with code_to_http_status, and stream to bounded_stream. These belong in separate commits with rationale; reviewers cannot cheaply separate value-changing edits from cosmetic ones.

issues.description: New POST tests assert status codes without naming the invariant under test
issues.detail: resp3 asserts 201 and resp4 asserts 400, but neither has a docstring stating the property being verified. The 400 outcome holds only because of the bounded_stream swap in the same PR, so the test pins an incidental implementation detail rather than a documented contract.

issues.description: FAQ snippet uses parenthesized assert(result.status == ...) which is a known Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(expr) reads like a function call and silently passes for tuples. Documentation code is read and copied carefully by newcomers; this should be assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400. Trivial fix but matters for an idiom-teaching FAQ.

issues.description: Omnibus test function bundles independent GET and POST cases with shared mutable state
issues.detail: test_things_advanced now mixes GET, two POSTs, and a malformed-length POST in one function. A failure in resp3 masks resp4 and shared app state couples cases. Splitting into named tests per assertion would make each invariant standalone and failures localized.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear verdict: this PR claims to add POST tests but quietly mutates the example under test (req.stream to req.bounded_stream) so that the new failing case becomes 400. Code and test were adjusted together without stating the underlying contract about Content-Length vs body length. The README diff additionally smuggles unrelated semantic changes (handler signature reorder, status formatting) under cosmetic reformatting, making correctness review difficult. The FAQ example fabricates the behavior it claims to demonstrate rather than teaching real Falcon semantics. Recommendation: name the Content-Length contract, isolate the bounded_stream swap with rationale, split the README into separate commits, and shrink the FAQ example to the one line that actually demonstrates header override.
